tweets.text:
Ahead of PCE next week, a reminder to keep an eye on the breadth of price increases.

At Jackson Hole in August, Chair Kevin Warsh said that “over the past 12 months, 54% of goods and services in the PCE basket showed price increases above 3%. This is well below the post-pandemic highs of about 77%, but it remains well above the level of 32% in the two decades that preceded the pandemic.”

Running the same exercise on the CPI across the roughly 180 item categories the BLS publishes, covering about 98% of the basket, yields mixed results.

While 47.2% of categories rose more than 3% from a year earlier in September, the lowest since December and down from 50.6% in August, that compares with an average of 31.7% from 2000 to 2019 although well off the peak of 80.4% in March 2022.

And weighted by share of spending, 62.2% of the basket is rising faster than 3%, the most since September 2025, up from 60.0% in August, as the categories that crossed above 3% included larger ones such as college tuition (+4.00%), hotels (+4.27%), cable, satellite and streaming TV (+3.33%) and motor vehicle repair (+3.55%), while eight of the 17 that fell back below 3% were grocery items.

The share above 5% rose to 23.0% of categories (13.1% of the basket) from 21.0% (11.6%), led by gasoline (+34.17%), hospital services (+5.63%), dental services (+6.02%) and airline fares (+22.45%), while 27.5% of categories are now falling from a year earlier, up from 21.0%.

The short silver trade is becoming crowded.

Silver's 3-month silver put-call skew is up to -3 points, its highest level since early July.

This metric measures the relative cost of put options to call options and is up +10 points over the last 4 weeks, signaling growing demand for bearish bets on silver prices.

Over the last 12 months, this metric has been higher only 2% of the time.

Meanwhile, speculative investors, including hedge funds and commodity trading advisers (CTAs), sold -$2.2 billion in silver futures over the 3 weeks ending October 13th.

As a result, their net long positioning is down to just +$1.7 billion, the lowest in at least 2 years.

For perspective, this metric stood at +$8.5 billion in December 2025.

Investors are extremely bearish on silver.

BREAKING: The average cost of a family’s annual health insurance premium in the US is up +$1,303 YoY, or +5%, to a record $28,303.

This marks the 4th consecutive annual increase of at least +$1,300.

Over this period, the average annual premium for family coverage has surged +$5,884, or +26%.

To put this into perspective, CPI inflation has risen +13% over the same period, or half as much.

Since 1999, the average health insurance premium for a family has soared +$22,494, or +387%.

This represents an average annual growth rate of +6.1%, well above CPI inflation at +2.6% over the same period.

Health insurance has never been more expensive.

Wall Street has a name for people who bet against stocks: intellectual cranks.

Jim Chanos's answer is simple. The indices go up over time. Most companies don't. They fail or get merged out of existence.

He thinks short sellers are born, not made. The research is the same but the temperament isn't.

Outside of tech, the payoff still has not shown up.

Revenue per worker is ripping for the Mag 7 and dead flat for the other 493. Profit margins, same split. And there is still no sign of AI lifting economy-wide productivity, which has gone nowhere for years.

The AI story gets settled in the S&P 493, not the Mag 7. So far the 493 shows nothing. That is the number that matters.

thread_tweets.text:
The AI boom is narrower than almost anyone admits.

The top 10% of firms account for 99.5% of all model-serving spend, 99% of neocloud, and 95%+ of OpenAI and Anthropic billings. And 80.4% of the heaviest AI spenders run on venture capital, not their own revenue.

This is a concentrated, circular buildout. A handful of companies are the entire trade.

tweets.text: Some focus on S&P 500 targets, others like to make sector calls, we focus on fundamental attributes to create baskets and recommend positioning. The upswing of eco and EPS data is where markets trade the most “risk-on.” That phase is now likely behind us. You can still be invested in the same themes across the cycle, but the same companies within those themes rarely outperform across the entire cycle. We’re a few months into the “higher-quality fundamentals” phase of the market cycle.
